subject: Re: Correcting for detection probability - at the species level

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: Correcting for detection probability - at the species level
parts:
Jeff, we generally recommend that you fit detection functions at the
species level. However, if all you need is abundance of all species
combined, it is OK to pool across species - that gives you a good estimate
of total abundance, but poor (biased) estimates of abundance by species.
This doesn't assume all species have the same detection function - it
relies on 'pooling robustness'. However, I would exclude any species that
are expected to be unusual in terms of detectability - e.g. exceptionally
cryptic species. Using the covariate model can help with rare species
relative to fitting each species independently, allowing you to include a
few more species in your analysis, but very rare species will remain
problematic.

Steve Buckland
